title: I Posted the BMX Pump-Track Hours After the Local Stacked Five Laps

parts.text: I rolled to the start gate at 5:08 p.m. and local Quin was already stacking laps on our numbered heat. The board said: ONE GATE. TWENTY MINUTES. FIVE LAPS MAX. I was twenty-five, track regular, holding a tag that listed our run. Quin shrugged. "Locals are the berms." I photographed the board, the tag, and his sixth lap on our roller. Then I asked for the heat log. At 5:16 parks pinged why Quin's name was on our five. I kept my voice track-loud enough and let the timestamp talk. A board is only a board until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Parks can see Quin's sixth lap on our roller during our heat.

social.video_title: He stacked six laps on our numbered heat — Part 1/2
social.description: Pump track, a local on our roller, a five-lap max he posted. I logged the sixth. Would you have asked for the heat log?

parts.text: Quin called it a pump until parks asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the sixth still. The gate went back to our tag. Quin ran his own twenty and told the next local atmosphere was always about rhythm. Rhythm is a word locals use when a board exists. Track policy now has a second line: LOCALS ARE NOT THE BERMS. I keep our tag on a labeled clip. Quin brown-bags his jokes. The track finally looks like a heat, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Heat log, numbered gate, and a second line on the board. Was a pump ever our sixth?
